(p-4936) Surah 34: Saba'

It was named after this because its narrative contains a verse indicating the bliss of Paradise in its breadth, its lack of hardship and its freedom from calamity, and its transformation into punishments for those who disbelieve in the Bestower of blessings. This is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an.

So said al-Muhaymili. It is Meccan, except that the verse ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see﴾ [Saba': 6] is excepted from it.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Farwa ibn Musaik al-Muradi, who said: "I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of God! Shall I not fight those among my people who have turned their backs?' The hadith... And in it: 'And there was revealed concerning Saba' what was revealed.' A man said: 'O Messenger of God! And what is Saba'?' The hadith..."

Ibn al-Hisar said: This indicates that this narrative is Medinan, because Farwa's migration was after the conversion of Thaqif in the ninth year.

He said: It is possible that his saying "and there was revealed" is a report of what had been revealed earlier, before his migration.

This was stated in (al-Itqan), and its number of verses is fifty-four.

(p-4937) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1] ﴿Praise be to God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter. And He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.﴾

﴿Praise be to God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ in creation, dominion, and disposal as He wills. ﴿And to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter's creation. Al-Shihab said: "The heavens and the earth are an expression for this whole world entire."

It includes worldly blessings. From the description by His saying "Who" (alladhi) etc., it is known that He is praised for the blessings of this world. When the second is restricted by being in the Hereafter, it is known that the first's place is this world, so the meaning becomes: He is the one praised for the blessings of this world in it, and for the blessings of the Hereafter in it. Or it is of the type of ihtibak, and its original form is: "Praise be to God etc. in this world, and to Him belongs what is in the Hereafter, and praise in it," so that what was omitted from the Hereafter is affirmed in each of them.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And to Him belongs praise﴾ is conjoined to the relative clause, or is a parenthetical insertion, if the clause "He knows" is a circumstantial clause. ﴿And He is the All-Wise﴾, i.e., He who perfected the affairs of both abodes and arranged them with His wisdom; ﴿the All-Aware﴾, i.e., aware of His creatures, their deeds, and their secrets. Then He mentioned, from what He encompasses in knowledge, His saying:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[2] ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is the Most Merciful, the Forgiving.﴾

﴿He knows what enters into the earth﴾ — that is, of rain, water, treasures, hidden things, and the dead. ﴿And what comes out of it﴾ — that is, of trees, plants, spring water, produce, and animals. (p-4938) ﴿And what descends from the sky﴾ — that is, of rain, snow, hail, thunderbolts, provisions, angels, and decrees. ﴿And what ascends into it﴾ — that is, of angels and the deeds of the servants. ﴿And He is the Most Merciful, the Forgiving﴾ — that is, toward whoever of the believers repents and fulfills the duty of gratitude to Him.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:

[3] ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you — the Knower of the unseen, from whom is not hidden an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and not what is smaller than that nor greater, except that it is in a clear register."﴾

﴿And those who disbelieve say﴾ meaning the polytheists of Makkah. ﴿The Hour will not come to us﴾ i.e., the Hour of recompense, denying it. ﴿Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you"﴾ i.e., the Hour. It is a rejection of their statement and an affirmation of what they negated, by swearing by Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿The Knower of the unseen﴾ is read in the genitive as an attribute (ṣifah), and in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject; and it has been recited as ﴿ʿAllāmi﴾ in the genitive. In this description there is a strengthening of the emphasis, because following the oath with the sublime attributes of the One sworn by indicates the grandeur of the matter sworn about, the strength of its affirmation and its truth, since it is in the position of calling upon testimony for the matter; especially when there is singled out from the attributes that which is specific to this meaning. For the establishment of the Hour is among the most famous of the unseen matters, and the most hidden of them and the first of them to rush to the heart. When it is said "Knower of the unseen," ﴿from whom is not hidden﴾ i.e., does not go absent, read with the zāy both pronounced and with a kasra: ﴿an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and not what is smaller than that nor greater, except that it is in a clear register﴾ i.e., all of it falls under His knowledge, so nothing is hidden from Him, however small it may be. As for the bones and the parts of the body, even if they have dissolved, scattered and been torn apart, He knows where they went and where they dispersed; then He will restore them as He originated them the first time, owing to the vastness of His knowledge and the greatness of His power, exalted is His majesty.

Subtleties:

The first: The majority of the reciters read ﴿aṣghar﴾ and ﴿akbar﴾ in the nominative, and there are two possibilities in this:

One: they are the subject (mubtada'), and the predicate is ﴿except in a clear register﴾. The second: they are coordinated (nasaq) with ﴿atom's weight﴾. On this basis, His words ﴿except in a clear register﴾ serve as an emphasis of the negation in ﴿does not go absent﴾, as if He said: "But it is in a clear register," and it occupies the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).

Some of the early generation read both with a fatḥah on the rāʾs, and there are two possibilities: One: that ﴿lā﴾ is the lā of absolution (lā al-tabri'ah), its noun built upon the fatḥah with it, and the predicate is His words ﴿except in a clear register﴾. The second: coordination with ﴿atom﴾, due to its being prohibited from nunation (tanwīn).

The second: His words, the Exalted, ﴿nor what is smaller than that﴾ indicate that ﴿atom's weight﴾ was not mentioned as a limit, rather what is smaller than it also does not go absent.

The third: al-Karkhi said: If it is asked, "What is the need to mention the greater?" For whoever knows the smaller than an atom must know the greater? The answer: Since Allah, the Exalted, intended to explain the establishment of matters in the Book, had He limited Himself to the smaller, someone might suppose that He records in it only the minor things because they are subject to forgetting, while the greater is not forgotten and so there is no need to record it. So He informed that recording in the Book is not so; for the greater is also written therein. And His words, the Exalted:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 34, verse 4:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds. Those will have forgiveness and a noble provision.﴾

﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾ is the reason (ʿillah) for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But the Hour will surely come upon you﴾ [Saba': 3], and an explanation of what its coming necessitates, namely the recompense of the doer of good and the doer of evil. ﴿Those will have forgiveness and a noble provision﴾ means: a pleasant life in the Hereafter.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5] ﴿Those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, for them is a painful punishment of severe torment.﴾

﴿Those who strive against Our signs﴾ means by disparaging them and attributing them to magic, poetry and other things. ﴿Seeking to frustrate﴾ means supposing, in their corrupt assumption and false conjecture, that they can prevail and render [the Prophet and the believers] powerless. ﴿For them is a punishment of torment (rijz)﴾, which is the worst of punishments; the ﴿min﴾ here is explanatory (li-l-bayan). ﴿Painful﴾: with the nominative (raf') it is an adjective of ﴿punishment﴾, and with the genitive (jarr) it is an adjective of ﴿torment﴾; these are two recitations (qira'atan).

It has been permitted regarding His saying ﴿Those who strive﴾ that it be a subject (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is the clause beginning ﴿those﴾ and what follows, and that it be conjoined (ma'tuf) to the preceding ﴿those who﴾, meaning: and He recompenses those who strive. In that case the clause ﴿those﴾ that follows would be a resumed sentence (mustaʼnafah), and the one before it a parenthetical insertion (mu'taridah).

Expressing their disparagement and obstruction as "striving" is a figurative depiction of their condition: the denier comes with concealing clear signs, so he needs a great striving and an intense, far-reaching diligence to promote his lie, perhaps he will frustrate the one who holds fast to it.

The discussion of the words of God, the Exalted:

[6–8] ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you that when you have been completely torn apart, you will be [recreated] in a new creation?"﴾ [Saba': 7] ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there in him madness?" Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and far error﴾ [Saba': 8].

﴿And see﴾, i.e., know: ﴿those who have been given knowledge, that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., His religion and His law. ﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ [Saba': 7], i.e., from the Quraysh: ﴿Shall we direct you to a man﴾ [Saba': 7], meaning the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿who will inform you that when you have been completely torn apart, you will be [recreated] in a new creation﴾ [Saba': 7], i.e., when you have been scattered in every manner of dispersal, to the extent that you have become dust and crumbled bone; ﴿you will be in a new creation﴾ [Saba': 7]. ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah﴾ [Saba': 8], i.e., in what he has said; ﴿or is there in him madness﴾ [Saba': 8], i.e., insanity by which he imagined that. He, the Exalted, refuted them regarding what revealed their evil condition, by His saying: ﴿Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and far error﴾ [Saba': 8], i.e., whose matter has reached its extreme. For whoever is called to righteousness and guidance, and to rejecting desire and corruption, and then accuses the caller of fabrication and madness, is deeply immersed in ignorance and has gone as far as possible in error. Then He indicated the magnitude of that great statement they uttered, and that it necessitates the descent of the most severe punishment, by His, glorified be He, saying:

(p-٤٩٤١) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We willed, We would cause the earth to swallow them, or make fragments of the sky fall upon them. Indeed, in that is a sign for every servant who turns back (to Allah) in repentance.﴾

﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We willed, We would cause the earth to swallow them, or make fragments of the sky fall upon them.﴾ That is: they are blind, so they did not look at the sky and the earth. Wherever they are, and wherever they travel, both of them (the sky and the earth) are before them and behind them, encompassing them. They cannot pass through their regions or go out from what they are in of the dominion (malakut) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And they did not fear that Allah would cause the earth to swallow them or make fragments of the sky fall upon them, because of their denial of the signs and their disbelief in the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and in what he brought, just as He did with Qarun and the companions of al-Aykah. This was conveyed by al-Zamakhshari.

(Al-Kisf): with a sukun on the sin, meaning "pieces" (al-qat'). It is either the plural of kisfah, or a verb in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ul), or a lightened form of the verbal noun. Hafs recited ﴿kisafan﴾ with a fatha: ﴿Indeed, in that﴾, i.e., in looking at the sky and the earth, reflecting upon them, and what they indicate of the power of Allah: ﴿is a sign﴾, i.e., a clear indication: ﴿for every servant who turns back﴾, i.e., who returns to his Lord and obeys Him, for his condition is never free of taking heed of His signs, and because He is capable of everything, including resurrection and the restoring of the decayed bones, as Allah, Exalted, said:

﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes indeed.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81] And Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know.﴾ [Ghafir: 57]

Then Allah, Exalted, informed of what He gave Dawud and Sulayman of favour, sovereignty, breadth of authority, abundance of troops, multitude of number and equipment, by the blessing of their turning back (to Allah) and their standing in thanks to the Lord, Exalted, as a promise to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his followers who turn back and give thanks, that they would attain the like of that, and as a reminder of His power over everything. So Allah, Exalted, said:

(p-4942) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[10–11] ﴿And We certainly bestowed upon David bounty from Us. "O mountains, sing back with him, and the birds." And We made iron soft for him, [saying], "Make full coats of mail and calculate well the links, and work righteousness. Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do."﴾ [Saba': 10–11].

﴿And We certainly bestowed upon David bounty from Us﴾ — i.e., "Repeat the glorification along with him." The phrase ﴿O mountains﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ﴿bounty﴾ or for ﴿We bestowed﴾, with the implied "Our saying" or "We said": "O mountains, sing back with him." ﴿And the birds﴾ is in the nominative or accusative case, coordinated (ʿatf) either with the wording of "the mountains" or with its grammatical position. Its accusative reading is also permitted as an object "with" (maf'ul maʿah), and it may be coordinated with ﴿bounty﴾ in the sense of "and We subjected the birds to him." Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, what is the difference between this arrangement and saying: "And We bestowed upon David bounty from Us, [causing] the mountains and the birds to sing back with him"? I say: How great is the difference between them! Do you not see the grandeur in it that is not hidden, in the indication of the might of Lordship and the majesty of Divinity, in that the mountains are made to occupy the position of rational beings who, when He commands them, obey and submit, and when He calls them, hear and respond? It is a signal that there is nothing among animate and inanimate, speaking and silent, but that it is subject to His will and not resistant to His decree. End of quote.

﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ — ﴿[saying], "Make full coats of mail"﴾ — i.e., wide coats of armor. ﴿And calculate well the links﴾ — i.e., be moderate in weaving the armor so that its rings are proportionate. ﴿And work righteousness﴾ — i.e., We said this to him and to his family. ﴿Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do﴾ — i.e., I will recompense you for it.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[12] ﴿And for Solomon, the wind; its morning course was a month's journey, and its evening course was a month's journey. And We caused a fountain of molten copper to flow for him. And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord. And whoever of them deviates from Our command, We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze.﴾

﴿And for Solomon﴾, i.e., We subjected for him: ﴿the wind; its morning course was a month's journey and its evening course was a month's journey﴾, i.e., its running in the morning was the distance of a month's journey, and its running in the evening was likewise. The wind (al-rih) is the air subjected between the sky and the earth. It is also used with the meanings of help (nusrah), guidance (dalalah), dominance (ghalabah) and strength (quwwah), as in the Qamus. ﴿And We caused a fountain of molten copper to flow for him﴾, i.e., the copper that is melted; that is, We made its spring flow for him, owing to the abundance of it that was available to him from the vastness of his kingdom. ﴿And among the jinn﴾, i.e., the powerful devils: ﴿those who worked before him﴾, i.e., at the erection of lofty buildings, the construction of palaces and other things: ﴿by the permission of his Lord﴾, i.e., by His command, exalted is He. ﴿And whoever of them deviates﴾, i.e., turns aside: ﴿from Our command, We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze﴾, i.e., the Fire. Then he detailed what was mentioned of their work with His words, exalted is He:

[13] "They made for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries (maḥārīb), statues (tamāthīl), basins like reservoirs, and cooking-pots fixed firmly in place. Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude. And few of My servants are truly grateful."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿They made for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries﴾, i.e., dwellings and noble assemblies, or mosques. ﴿And statues﴾, i.e., pictures and varied engravings upon the walls, the ceilings, and the pillars. It is the plural of (timthāl), which is everything fashioned in the likeness of something else, whether of an animal or of a non-animal. The making of images was not forbidden at that time.

As-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): Ibn al-Faras said: a group has used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of depiction, but it is prohibited, for it was abrogated in our law. ﴿And basins like reservoirs﴾, i.e., troughs like large cisterns. (Al-jifān) is the plural of (jafnah), which, like the saḥfah and the qaṣʿah, is any vessel in which food is placed, in general. It is said that the jafnah is the largest of the bowls, followed by the qaṣʿah, which feeds ten, then the saḥfah, which feeds five, then the mīkalah, which feeds three or two, then the ṣaḥīfah. ﴿And cooking-pots fixed firmly in place﴾, i.e., steadfast upon their stones, not moved from them because of their size. ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude﴾, i.e., it was said to them: work for God and worship Him in the manner of thanks for His bounties. In this is an indication that work should be for the sake of gratitude, not out of hope or fear, just as it indicates the obligation of gratitude, and that it is done through action and is not confined to the tongue; for its reality is the servant's directing of all that God has bestowed upon him toward that for which it was created. Dawud, peace be upon him, may be included here in (the family); for the family of a man may include him. ﴿And few of My servants are truly grateful﴾, i.e., those who devote most of their time to fulfilling gratitude with their hearts, tongues and limbs.

(p-4944) Discourse on the interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying:

[14] ﴿Then when We decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. So when he fell down, the jinn saw clearly that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating torment.﴾

﴿Then when We decreed death for him﴾, that is, for Solomon, ﴿death﴾, ﴿nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth﴾, which is the termite (al-aradah), ﴿eating away at his staff﴾, that is, his rod by which he would have it "yansa'" (postpone and delay), meaning he would drive away and defer. ﴿So when he fell down, the jinn saw clearly that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating torment﴾, that is, the severe [labor] of continuing to work as he had set it for them and persisting at it, because they thought he was alive.

Then, after explaining the condition of the grateful ones regarding these blessings, the Exalted made clear, from the reports about some of the disbelievers in His blessings, what contains admonition and lesson, with His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the Exalted's saying:

[15] ﴿There was indeed for Sheba in their dwelling a sign: two gardens, on the right and on the left. "Eat of the provision of your Lord and be thankful to Him. A good land and a Forgiving Lord."﴾

﴿There was indeed for Sheba﴾: Sheba is the name of an ancestor of a tribe. It has also been read with diptotic inflection (ghayr munsarif, i.e. not taking tanwin), as the name of a place: ﴿in their dwelling﴾, meaning in the places where they lived. It is in Yemen and is called (Ma'rib), like a dwelling-place in the lands of the Azd, at the far end of the mountains of Hadramawt. In earlier times it was the capital of the Tubba' (the Himyarite kings), for it is the city of Bilqis, about four stages (marahil) distant from San'a'. It has also been read as ﴿masakinihim﴾ (their dwellings). ﴿A sign﴾ of His power and of His requiting the wrongdoer. ﴿Two gardens, on the right and on the left﴾: that is, two groups of orchards, on the right of their town and on its left; or, each one of them had two gardens, on the right of his dwelling and on its left. It was said to them: ﴿Eat of the provision of your Lord and be thankful to Him﴾, that is, by directing what He has bestowed upon you to the purpose for which He created it.

Then He made clear what necessitates the thanks commanded, by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿A good land﴾, that is, pleasant, beautiful, blessed, with no blight in it. ﴿And a Forgiving Lord﴾, that is, to those who give thanks to Him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 34, verse 16:

(p-4945) The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[16] ﴿But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of al-Arim, and We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a few lote-trees.﴾

﴿But they turned away﴾ i.e., from gratitude. ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of al-Arim﴾ i.e., the flood of the severe matter, that is, the harsh [torrent] and the violent rain; or the valley; or the dam that holds back the water; or it is the sturdy structure built between two mountains to conserve and store rainwater, in which openings were left in the measure of what they needed for their irrigation. When they transgressed, Allah destroyed them by the ruin of this structure, and its torrent of water poured down upon them, drowning their lands, corrupting their habitations and their soil, and those among them who survived were compelled to flee from them. As the Exalted said: ﴿And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit﴾ i.e., fruit that is bitter, or repulsive and not edible; ﴿and tamarisk﴾, a tree resembling the tamarisk among the trees of the desert, which bears no fruit; ﴿and a few lote-trees﴾, which is the tree of the nabq (jujube); i.e., a meagre quantity that neither fattens nor satisfies hunger. This is the exchange of blessings for calamities for those who do not give thanks for blessings, as the Exalted said:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[17] ﴿That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief. And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾

﴿That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief. And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾ That is: for their ingratitude for the blessings, or for their turning away from following the messengers and denying the truth, and their inclining toward the people of falsehood. Then He, glory be to Him, explained what they were in of blessing, comfort, pleasant living, secure lands, and connected towns, by His saying, glory be to Him:

ٱلْقَوْلُ فِي تَأْوِيلِ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى:

[ ١٨ ] ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْقُرَى الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا قُرًى ظَاهِرَةً وَقَدَّرْنَا فِيهَا السَّيْرَ سِيرُوا فِيهَا لَيَالِيَ وَأَيَّامًا آمِنِينَ﴾.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْقُرَى الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا﴾ أي: بِالزُّرُوعِ وَالثِّمَارِ، وَحُسْنِ الْعُمْرَانِ، وَهِيَ (p-٤٩٤٦) قُرًى بِصَنْعَاءَ، كَمَا قَالَهُ مُجَاهِدٌ، وَسَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، وَمَالِكٌ، وَغَيْرُهُمْ: ﴿قُرًى ظَاهِرَةً﴾ أي: مُتَوَاصِلَةً، يُرَى بَعْضُهَا مِنْ بَعْضٍ لِتَقَارُبِهَا؛ فَهِيَ ظَاهِرَةٌ لِأَعْيُنِ النَّاظِرِينَ، أَوْ ظَاهِرَةٌ لِلْمُسَافِرِينَ لَا تَبْعُدُ عَنْ مَسَالِكِهِمْ: ﴿وَقَدَّرْنَا فِيهَا السَّيْرَ﴾ أي: جَعَلْنَا بَيْنَ قُرَاهَا مَقَادِيرَ مُتَسَاوِيَةً، فَمَنْ سَارَ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ صَبَاحًا وَصَلَ إِلَى أُخْرَى وَقْتَ الظَّهِيرَةِ وَالْقَيْلُولَةِ، وَمَنْ سَارَ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ وَصَلَ إِلَى أُخْرَى عِنْدَ الْغُرُوبِ، فَلَا يَحْتَاجُ لِحَمْلِ زَادٍ وَلَا مَبِيتٍ فِي أَرْضٍ خَالِيَةٍ، وَلَا يَخَافُ مِنْ عَدُوٍّ وَنَحْوِهِ: ﴿سِيرُوا فِيهَا لَيَالِيَ وَأَيَّامًا آمِنِينَ﴾ أي: لَا تَخَافُونَ فِي اللَّيْلِ أَوِ النَّهَارِ، أَوْ وَإِنْ تَطَاوَلَ أَمَدُ سَفَرِكُمْ فِيهَا وَامْتَدَّ، فَلَا تَرَوْنَ إِلَّا الْأَمْنَ، وَالْأَمْرُ عَلَى تَقْدِيرِ الْقَوْلِ بِلِسَانِ الْمَقَالِ بِوَاسِطَةِ نَبِيٍّ وَنَحْوِهِ، أَوْ بِلِسَانِ الْحَالِ، كَأَنَّهُمْ لَمَّا تَمَكَّنُوا مِنْهُ جُعِلُوا مَأْمُورِينَ بِهِ، فَالْأَمْرُ لِلْإِبَاحَةِ. وَفِي: (فِي)، إِشْعَارٌ بِشِدَّةِ الْقُرْبِ، حَتَّى كَأَنَّهُمْ لَمْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْ نَفْسِ الْقُرَى.

The Qur'an verse on the composition of this verse is:

**Verse 19:** ﴿So they said, "Our Lord, make the distance between our journeys longer," and they wronged themselves. So We made them tales, and We scattered them completely. Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful person.﴾

﴿So they said﴾, meaning by the tongue of their state and their inclination toward the destructive Satanic paths: ﴿"Our Lord, make the distance between our journeys longer"﴾, meaning they prepared themselves for their misguidance and disbelief, so that their places would be made such that mounts and riding beasts would be needed to cover the distance between them and where they traveled. This came about through what they exchanged for their good lands. ﴿And they wronged themselves﴾, meaning until what befell them befell them. ﴿So We made them tales﴾, meaning people speak of them and marvel at their news, and at how Allah plotted against them, and scattered their union after gathering and pleasant living. ﴿And We scattered them completely﴾, meaning We dispersed them in every kind of dispersal, until people took them as a proverb struck. They say: "They scattered as the hands of Saba'" and "They went as the hands of Saba'," with a shortened alif.

Al-Azhari said: The Arabs do not hamz (glottalize) Saba' in this context, because it became common in their speech and they found the hamza burdensome in it, even though its origin is hamzated. "Dhahaba" (went) is known. "Al-Ayadi" is the plural of "ayd," and "al-Aydi" is the plural of "yad" (hand). It has the meanings of the limb, of blessing, and of a path, and the last is what is meant here (p-4947). In al-Tahdhib he said: Their saying "dhahabu ayadi Saba'" means "scattered." They were compared to the people of Saba' when Allah scattered them throughout the earth in every kind of dispersal, so each group took a separate path. And "al-yad" means the path. It is said: "The people took the way of the sea." So when people went in different directions, it was said: "They went as the hands of Saba'," meaning their paths scattered them, as the people of Saba' scattered into various directions.

Ibn Malik said: It is a compound structure like "fifteen," built on sukun. In *Zahr al-Akam fi al-Amthal wa al-Hikam* it is mentioned that Saba' was the most fertile of Allah's lands, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Two gardens, on the right and on the left﴾ [Saba': 15]. It was said that its extent was a month's journey for a diligent rider, and a walker would traverse the gardens from their beginning to their end without ever leaving the shade, with water gushing, rivers clear, and the open land wide. They remained for a time in security, with no one defying them without being broken. At the beginning of the matter, floods would overwhelm it. So Himyar gathered the people of its kingdom and consulted them, and they built a dam at the start of the flow of water, paved it with stones and iron, and made openings in it for the water. When the floods came they were divided in a way that their benefit reached all of them in the gardens and the cultivated lands. But when they disbelieved in the blessings of Allah the Exalted, and saw that their kingdom could not be destroyed by anything, and worshipped the sun, Allah sent a mouse against their dam, and it broke through it. He sent the flood upon them, and it scattered them completely, destroyed their green land, and they dispersed throughout the lands. The Azd joined Oman, Khuza'a joined Batn Murr, al-Aws and al-Khazraj joined Yathrib, the family of Jafna joined the land of al-Sham, and the family of Judhaymah al-Abrash joined Iraq.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Abbas that a man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Saba': "What is it? A man, a woman, or a land?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, it is a man who had ten sons. Six of them settled in Yemen, and four in al-Sham. As for the Yemenis, they are Madhhij, Kindah, al-Azd, al-Ash'ariyyun, Anmar, and Himyar. As for the Shamiyyah, they are Lakhm, Judham, Amilah, and Ghassan." Ibn Kathir said: Its chain is good, except for Ibn Lahi'ah.

Imam Ahmad also narrated from Farwah ibn Musayk, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah! Shall I fight with the front of my people against their rear?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes. So fight with the front of your people against their rear." When I turned away, he called me and said: "Do not fight them until you call them to Islam." (p-4948) I said: "O Messenger of Allah! What about Saba'? Is it a valley, a mountain, or what?" He (ﷺ) said: "No, rather it is a man from the Arabs who had ten sons. Six of them went rightward (toward good fortune), and four went leftward (toward ill fortune). The rightward were al-Azd, al-Ash'ariyyun, Himyar, Kindah, Madhhij, Anmar, who are called Bajilah, and Khath'am. The leftward were Lakhm, Judham, Amilah, and Ghassan."

Ibn Kathir said: It is a good hadith, although Abu Hubab al-Kalbi is in its chain, and they have spoken about him.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated it in the book *al-Qasd wa al-Umam bi Ma'rifat Usul Ansab al-Arab wa al-Ajam* from Tamim al-Dari: "that a man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Saba'," and he mentioned the like of it.

Ibn Kathir said: So this hadith is strengthened and becomes good.

Genealogists, among them Muhammad ibn Ishaq, mentioned the name of Saba': Abd Shams ibn Yashjub ibn Ya'rub ibn Qahtan. He was called Saba' because he was the first to take captives (sabi) among the Arabs. He was also called al-Ra'ish, because he was the first to take booty in raids and gave it to his people, so he was named al-Ra'ish, and the Arabs call wealth "rish" and "riyash." They also mentioned that he gave good news of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his earlier time, and he said in that regard a poem:

Soon a great king will rule after us, a prophet who does not permit what is forbidden,
And after him will rule among them kings who submit to him every leader,
And after them will rule among us kings, and rule among us will pass by division,
And after Qahtan will rule a prophet, pious, devoted, the best of mankind,
He will be named Ahmad. Would that I could live a year after his mission,
So I would support him and give him my aid, with every armored warrior and every archer.
When he appears, be his helpers, and whoever meets him, convey my greeting to him.

Al-Hamdani mentioned this in the book *al-Iklil*. They differed about Qahtan. It was said: he is of the lineage of Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh. It was said: of the lineage of Abir, who is Hud, peace be upon him. It was said: he is of the lineage of Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Khalil, peace and blessings be upon them both. Imam al-Hafiz Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr al-Namari has mentioned this in detail in the book *al-Inbah ala Dhikr Usul al-Qaba'il al-Ruwah* (p-4949). Ibn Kathir said: The meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) statement about Saba' that "he was a man from the Arabs," meaning the Ancient Arabs (al-Arab al-Aribah), who existed before al-Khalil, peace be upon him, from the lineage of Sam ibn Nuh. And according to the third view, he was of the lineage of al-Khalil, peace be upon him, but this is not well known among them. And Allah knows best.

However, in Sahih al-Bukhari it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by a group of men from Aslam who were shooting arrows and said: "Shoot, O sons of Isma'il, for your father was an archer." Aslam is a tribe of the Ansar. The Ansar, both al-Aws and al-Khazraj, are from the Arabs of Yemen, from Saba', who settled in Yathrib when they were dispersed, as has passed.

Then he said: The meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) statement "he had ten sons" is that these ten were from his descendants, and that the origins of the tribes of the Arabs of Yemen return to them, not that they were born from his loins. Rather, some of them were connected to him through two or three generations, and some more or fewer, as is established and clarified in its places in the books of genealogy.

﴿Indeed in that﴾, meaning in what has been mentioned of their story, and what befell them of vengeance and punishment, and the change of blessings and the transformation of well-being due to what they committed of disbelief and sins: ﴿are signs﴾, meaning great lessons. ﴿For every patient, grateful person﴾, meaning whose character is patience over desires, passions, and sins, and gratitude for blessings. Al-A'sha said in a qasidah:

In that is an example for the one who takes warning, and Ma'rib, which the flood of al-Arim has obliterated,
A marble structure Himyar built for them, which did not shift when its flood came,
It gave drink to their crops and vines, despite their abundant water when it was divided,
So they became scattered hands, none of whom could drink from it what a weaned child could drink.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[20–21] ﴿And Iblis had indeed found his assumption about them to be true, so they followed him, except for a group of the believers.﴾ ﴿And he had no authority over them, except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is Guardian over all things.﴾ [Saba': 21].

﴿And Iblis had indeed found his assumption about them to be true﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: It was recited as ṣaddaqa, with and without the shaddah (intensive doubling), with Iblis in the nominative and al-Ẓann (the assumption) in the accusative. As for the one who doubles the letter, it means: "he verified his assumption concerning them, and found his assumption to be true." That is, ṣaddaqa here means ḥaqqaqa (verified) metaphorically, because he assumed something and it happened, so he verified it.

And his saying: "or he found his assumption to be true," for the Arabs say ṣaddaqaka ẓannuka ("your assumption proved true for you"). The meaning is that Iblis would present to him, through his assumption, something about them, and when it occurred, it was as if he had confirmed it. End of Shihab's words.

As for the one who reads it without the shaddah, it means: "he spoke the truth in his assumption, or he spoke truly while assuming an assumption," like the phrase fa'altahu jahdaka ("I did it with your full effort"). That is, ẓannahu (his assumption) is in the accusative as an adverb of place by removal of the preposition (naz' al-khāfid, removal of the governing preposition), and its original form is fī ẓannihi ("in his assumption"). That is, he found his assumption to be correct in reality, so ṣaddaqa in that case means aṣāba (hit the mark) metaphorically. Or it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar) of an implied verb, like fa'altahu jahdaka, meaning "while you exert your effort." Thus the verbal noun and its governing verb stand in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). End of Shihab's words.

With Iblis in the accusative and al-Ẓann in the nominative: with the shaddah, it means "he found his assumption to be true." Without the shaddah, it means "his assumption spoke the truth to him when his seduction of them was imagined to him," with Ighwā'uhum (their seduction) in the nominative as the subject, or in the accusative by elision and transitivization (ḥadhf wal-iysāl), with its subject being the pronoun of the assumption; that is, "their seduction was imagined to him." End of Shihab's words. They say: ṣadaqaka ẓannuka ("your assumption proved true for you").

With the non-doubled form and both nouns in the nominative, meaning that al-Ẓann is substituted for Iblis by substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). End of Shihab's words. The meaning is: "the assumption of Iblis proved true concerning them." End quote.

This may be either his assumption about Saba', when he saw them immersed in their desires, or his assumption about the children of Adam, when he saw the desire and anger that had been placed within them.

﴿so they followed him, except for a group of the believers﴾ ﴿And he had no authority over them, except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it﴾ [Saba': 21]. That is: he had no power or dominance over them through whispering and misleading, except for a sound purpose and a clear wisdom. That is so that the believer in the Hereafter may be distinguished from the one who doubts it. He explained the empowerment by knowledge, and the intended meaning is what knowledge is connected to. This was said by al-Zamakhshari. He means that the future knowledge that is given as the reason here is not the eternal knowledge that subsists in the Most Holy Essence, but rather its connection to the known in the world of witnessing, upon which reward and punishment through recompense are based.

So the meaning is: We did not empower him over them except so that what We knew of the hidden might come forth, and thus the wisdom in it would appear through the realization of what We intended of recompense, or of its necessary consequence, which is the manifestation of what is known.

It is also possible that the meaning is: so that We may recompense for faith and its opposite. Thus it is in al-Ināyah. ﴿And your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾ [Saba': 21], that is, watchful and standing over their conditions and their affairs.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[22] ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any share in them, nor is there for Him any helper among them.﴾

﴿Say﴾: i.e., to the polytheists, to manifest the falsehood of what they hold, and to rebuke them. ﴿Call upon those whom you claim﴾: i.e., whom you have claimed to be gods, ﴿besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight﴾: i.e., of good or evil, benefit or harm, ﴿in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any share in them﴾: i.e., any partnership, neither in creation, nor in ownership, nor in management. ﴿Nor is there for Him any helper among them﴾: i.e., any supporter who assists Him in the management of His creation. Al-Zamakhshari said: He means that they, in this matter, are in a state of incapacity and remoteness from the attributes of lordship. So how is it valid that they should be called upon as He is called upon, or hoped in as He is hoped in?

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 34, verse 23:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He permits, until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they say, "What has your Lord said?" They say, "The truth; and He is the Most High, the Grand."﴾

﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He permits﴾ That is: of those deserving the station of intercession (p-4952), such as the prophets and the angels. This is a refutation of their saying, "These are our intercessors with Allah." ﴿Until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾ That is: the terror is lifted from the hearts of the intercessors and of those for whom intercession is made, by a word spoken by the Lord of Might when He grants permission. Upon this they rejoice. ﴿They say﴾ That is: asking one another, ﴿"What has your Lord said?" They say, "The truth"﴾ That is: He has spoken the true word, which is the permission for intercession for whomever He approves. ﴿And He is the Most High, the Grand﴾ That is: He is the Possessor of loftiness and greatness; no king or prophet may speak except by His permission, nor intercede except for whomever He approves.

Ibn Kathir said: This is also a lofty station in greatness: when He, exalted is He, speaks by revelation, the people of the heavens hear His speech and are seized with trembling from awe, until there overtakes them something like a swoon. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and Masruq, and others.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, "With what is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾ connected, and why is 'until' used as a limit?" I say: it is connected to what is understood from this speech, namely that there is a waiting for permission, an expectation, a delay and a fear on the part of those who hope for intercession and the intercessors, as to whether they will be permitted or not, and that permission is not granted except after a long time and a prolonged period of waiting. A state like this is indicated by His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful; they have no power to address Him﴾ [An-Naba': 37] ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows, they will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is right﴾ [An-Naba': 38]. That is: if intercession is for one whom He permits in such a state, in greatness and exaltedness from the Majestic One, how can an inanimate object that does not understand obtain it, especially when it is an enemy of the Great, the Exalted? Thus their lie concerning them, that they are intercessors, and their deprivation of that station, become clear in the plainest explanation and the most eloquent statement.

There is another interpretation of the verse: the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾ is: from the hearts of the polytheists at the time of death, and on the Day of Resurrection when they awaken from the heedlessness they were in during the world, and their intellects return to them on the Day of Resurrection, they say, "What has your Lord said?" It is said to them, "The truth," and they are informed of what they were heedless of in the world. Mujahid said: ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾ means: the veil is lifted from them on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said: that is, it is lifted from what is in them of doubt and denial. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam (p-4953) said: this is at death; they acknowledge when acknowledgment no longer benefits them. Ibn Jarir preferred the first view, that the pronoun refers to the angels.

Ibn Kathir said: This is the truth about which there is no doubt, because of the soundness of the hadiths and reports on it, and because of the arrival of what supports it in another verse, and the Qur'an explains part of itself by part, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they do not intercede except for one whom He approves, and they are fearful of His awe﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 28]. Indeed, the noble text does not reject what they mentioned, but observing similar and parallel passages is the foundation in the field of understanding interpretation, wherever a way to them is found.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 34, verse 24:

The discussion of the interpretation of His statement, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?" Say: "Allah. And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in manifest error."﴾

﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?"﴾ This is a command to rebuke the polytheists, by compelling them to acknowledge that their gods do not possess an atom's weight in either of them. His statement, ﴿Say: "Allah"﴾, means: He whom you acknowledge to be the Creator, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, or who controls hearing and sight, and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and who arranges the affair?" They will say, "Allah."﴾ [Yunus: 31]. That is: then the proof was established against them from themselves.

﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in manifest error.﴾ That is: and indeed one of the two parties, namely the monotheists who worship the One who provides from the heavens and the earth, or those of them who associate with Him inanimate objects that cannot be described as having power over an atom, are surely upon one of the two matters: guidance or error.

al-Zamakhshari said: This is from the fair speech, such that everyone who hears it, whether a supporter or an opponent, says to the one addressed by it: "Your companion has been fair to you." And in its place, after the presentation of what was presented of the eloquent affirmation, there is an indication, not hidden, as to who is of the two parties upon guidance and who is in manifest error. But indirect allusion and concealment are better for bringing the disputant to the goal, and more effective in overcoming him while keeping the opponent's clamor minimal and blunting his strength with ease. Similar to this is the saying of a man to his companion: "The knowledge of God is that I and you are truthful, and indeed one of us is a liar." 

From this is the verse of Hassan:

*Do you satirize him, when you are not his equal? Then your evil and his good shall be ransomed.*

End of quotation.

al-Nasir said: This is a refined interpretation and a sweet, graceful turn of expression. I repeated it to my hearing and it gained brilliance through repetition, and the mind retained it, as if I were slow in understanding when it conveys meaning. After this, one should not object to the method that the later jurists frequently employ in their disputations and discussions, namely their saying: "One of the two matters is necessarily true in an ambiguous manner." So this course, in this valley, is not far off. Reflect upon it, and God is the Granter of success. End of quotation.

al-Shihab said: This is one of the arts of eloquence, called (the fair speech). It has been said that the verse is in the figure of *laff wa nashr* (folding and unfolding) in ordered sequence. It was objected that if the folding were intended, such that "upon guidance" refers to "we" and "in error" refers to "you," then the conjunction would be with *wa* rather than *aw*, and that *aw* being used in the sense of *wa*, as in the saying of the poet:

*Equal are the breaking of his bread, or the breaking of a bone from his bones*

is very far-fetched. However, it has been said: if an allusion to that were placed in it, it would not be far-fetched. The choice of (upon, *ʿalā*) for guidance, and (in, *fī*) for its counterpart, serves to indicate the elevation of the possessor of guidance, his firmness, and his awareness of what he intends, like one standing on a high place or riding a steed; and the immersion of the one astray in his error, until it is as if he were in a dark pit.

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we have committed as sin, nor will we be asked about what you do.﴾

﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we have committed as sin, nor will we be asked about what you do.﴾ That is: Say to these polytheists: you will not be asked about the sin we committed, nor about the transgression we incurred; and we will not be asked about the deeds you do.

Ibn Kathir said: Its meaning is disavowal of them. That is: you are not of us, nor are we of you. Rather, we invite you to God, exalted is He, and to His Oneness, and to devoting worship to Him alone. If you respond, then you are of us and we are of you; and if you deny, then we are free of you and you are free of us. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they deny you, say: To me is my deed, and to you is your deed. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do﴾ [Yunus: 41]. And His saying: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ [al-Kafirun: 1] ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ [al-Kafirun: 2] ﴿nor will you worship what I worship﴾ [al-Kafirun: 3], the surah. End of quote.

What he mentioned is a subtle meaning, which few perceive. I call it "tafsir by resemblances and parallels" (al-tafsir bi'l-ashbah wa'l-nazha'ir), which is taking a concise or general verse to a similar verse that is elaborated or clarified. Only one firmly grounded in the art of interpretation (ta'wil), and devoted to reflecting on the revelation (tanzil), grasps this. Among the subtleties of the verse is what al-Zamakhshari and al-Muntasif mentioned: that this statement is more equitable than the first, in that it attributes the sin (ijram) to the self, and means by it the slips and minor faults from which no believer is free; and it attributes the deed to the addressees, and means by it disbelief, acts of disobedience and major sins. Thus it expresses trivial lapses with what is used for grave matters, and grave matters with what is used for lapses, out of commitment to equity. Moreover, it mentions the sin attributed to the self in the past tense (al-madi), which gives the meaning certainty, whereas for the deed attributed to the opponent it uses a form that does not give that certainty. And God knows best.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Saying, Exalted is He:

[26] ﴿Say: Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us with truth, and He is the Judge, the All-Knowing.﴾

﴿Say: Our Lord will gather us together﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, in one place. ﴿Then He will judge between us with truth﴾, meaning: He will decide with justice, because one of the two groups is upon guidance and the other upon misguidance. On that Day the guided one among us will be distinguished from the astray, and He will recompense each one according to his deeds, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And on the day the Hour comes, that Day they will be divided﴾ [al-Rum: 14]. ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, delighted﴾ [al-Rum: 15]. ﴿But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought forth into punishment﴾ [al-Rum: 16]. For this reason He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And He is the Judge, the All-Knowing﴾, meaning: the Ruler, the Just, the All-Knowing of the judgment between His creatures, because nothing hidden is concealed from Him, and He has no need of witnesses to make known to Him the one who is right from the one who is in the wrong.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿Say: "Show me those you have attached to Him as partners. No! Rather, He is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise."﴾

﴿Say: "Show me those you have attached to Him as partners."﴾ That is: you made them rivals (andad) to Allah and set them up as equals to Him. Abu al-Su'ud said: The purpose of their command to show the idols, while they were in plain view of him, peace and blessings be upon him, is to make manifest their great error and to make them aware of the falsity of their opinion. That is: "Show them to me so that I may look at what quality you attached them to God, He to whom nothing is like, in deserving worship." This also adds further rebuke to them after the proof has been established against them.

The grammarian (al-Mu'rib) has permitted, in (ra'a) here, that it be a cognitive verb (ilmiyyah) transitive to three objects by the hamzat al-naql (causative hamza): the ya' of the speaker, the relative pronoun, and "their partners" (shurakha'uhu). The returning pronoun of the relative is omitted; that is: "you attached them." And it may be a visual verb (basriyyah) transitive to two objects by the causative: the ya' of the speaker and the relative pronoun, with "partners" as a circumstantial accusative (hal). There is no weakness in this, as Ibn 'Atiyyah said. Rather, there is in it a rebuke for them, since its literal meaning is not intended; for he used to see them and know them. So it is a metaphor and an image. The meaning: "If what you claimed as a partner were displayed to the eyes, and it is wood and stone, your disgrace would be complete."

His words, exalted is He: ﴿No!﴾ are a restraint on them from associating partners, after the refutation of the comparison. ﴿Rather, He is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ That is: He who is described with overpowering dominion and manifest wisdom. Where, then, are their partners, which are the basest and most lowly of things, compared with this lofty station? The pronoun refers either to Allah, mighty and exalted, or to a matter (sha'n). So said Abu al-Su'ud.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 34, verse 28:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind, as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of mankind do not know.﴾

﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind, as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of mankind do not know.﴾ That is: We have not sent you except as a general mission for all creatures among those who are accountable, bringing good tidings to whoever obeys you of Paradise, and warning whoever disobeys you of the Fire, like His saying, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all collectively﴾ [al-A'raf: 158] ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1].

﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ That is: their ignorance leads them to what they are in of error and misguidance, like the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you should strive eagerly, are not believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103] ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 116].

Ibn Abbas said, as related by Ibn Abi Hatim: Indeed Allah, exalted is He, preferred Muhammad (ﷺ) over the people of the heavens and over the prophets. They said: "O son of Abbas! In what did Allah prefer him over the prophets?" He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Indeed Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, to make clear to them﴾ [Ibrahim: 4] (p-4958), and He said to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾, so Allah, exalted is He, sent him to the jinn and mankind.

Ibn Kathir said: What Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said has been established in the two Sahihs, traced back to the Prophet, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things which none of the prophets before me were given: I was supported with awe for a distance of a month's journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification, so whichever man of my nation is overtaken by the prayer, let him pray; spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and they were not lawful for anyone before me; I have been given intercession; and every prophet used to be sent only to his own people, while I have been sent to all mankind." And in the Sahih also, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been sent to the red and the black." Mujahid said: this means the jinn and mankind. Others said: it means the Arabs and the non-Arabs. The verification of the meaning of the generality of his mission and the comprehensiveness of his prophethood is that he came with a Law that fits the interests and needs of people wherever they are and in whatever time they exist, which no law before it had ever agreed upon; and for this reason the prophethoods were sealed with his prophethood (ﷺ), as has been established in its proper place.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[29-30] ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿Say, "For you is the appointment of a Day from which you will not remain behind an hour, nor will you precede it."﴾ [Saba': 30].

(p-4959) ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿Say, "For you is the appointment of a Day from which you will not remain behind an hour, nor will you precede it."﴾ [Saba': 30]. They mean by "the promise" that with which they were warned, mockingly, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [al-Shura: 18], and His saying: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a term already counted﴾ [Hud: 104], ﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them will be wretched and happy﴾ [Hud: 105].

They mean by "the promise" that with which they were warned, mockingly, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [al-Shura: 18], and His saying: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a term already counted﴾ [Hud: 104], ﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them will be wretched and happy﴾ [Hud: 105].

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[31] ﴿Those who disbelieve say, "We will never believe in this Qur'an or in that which came before it." If only you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, sending back words to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers."﴾

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "We will never believe in this Qur'an or in that which came before it"﴾: that is, what was revealed before the Qur'an of His Books. ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, sending back words to one another﴾: that is, they pull at the ends of the conversation and return it among themselves. Then he put in apposition (badal, a grammatical term meaning a substituted noun that restates the earlier one) for "sending back" his saying: ﴿Those who were oppressed will say﴾, and they are the followers, ﴿to those who were arrogant﴾, and they are their leaders and chiefs, ﴿Were it not for you, we would have been believers.﴾

The discussion of the words of His, the Exalted:

[32] ﴿Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Is it we who averted you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals."﴾.

﴿Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Is it we who averted you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals."﴾ That is: we did not do to you more than that we called you and you followed us without proof or evidence, and you opposed the proofs, the evidences, and the arguments that the Messengers brought, out of your own desires and your own choice for that.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[ 33 ] ﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was your scheming by night and day, when you were commanding us to disbelieve in God and to set up equals with Him." And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment. We will place shackles around the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾.

﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was your scheming by night and day"﴾: i.e., your scheming in them, your inciting us, and your wishful thinking for us. ﴿"when you were commanding us to disbelieve in God and to set up equals with Him"﴾: i.e., counterparts and deities besides Him. ﴿And they will conceal their regret﴾: i.e., all of them, the leaders and the followers. ﴿when they see the punishment. We will place shackles around the necks of those who disbelieved﴾: and these are the chains that join their hands with their necks. ﴿Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾: i.e., for their deeds, each according to his measure. For the leaders there is a punishment proportionate to them, and for the followers a punishment proportionate to them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 34, verses 34–35:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[34–35] ﴿And We did not send a warner into any town but that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent."﴾ ﴿And they said, "We are greater in wealth and children, and we will not be punished."﴾ [Saba': 35] I.e., they claimed that Allah had honoured them with that in this world, so He would not punish them in the Hereafter, supposing it to occur; and they imagined that, had they not been honoured by Allah, He would not have provided for them, and that, had the believers not been despised by Him, He would not have deprived them. [34–35] ﴿And We did not send a warner into any town but that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent."﴾ ﴿And they said, "We are greater in wealth and children, and we will not be punished."﴾ [Saba': 35] I.e., they claimed that Allah had honoured them with that in this world, so He would not punish them in the Hereafter, supposing it to occur; and they imagined that, had they not been honoured by Allah, He would not have provided for them, and that, had the believers not been despised by Him, He would not have deprived them. (p-4961) The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[36] ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it. But most of mankind do not know."﴾

﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it"﴾, i.e., He restricts it for him according to what His wisdom and His will concerning His servants require, [He extends it to] whomever He loves and [restricts it for] whomever He does not love. He is most knowing of its requirements and its affairs. Therefore, the matter of reward and punishment, whose criterion is obedience and its absence, should not be measured by this. For this reason He said: ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ that. They presume that the basis of expansion is honor and the basis of restriction is humiliation, and they are ignorant that the criterion of success and nearness to Him, exalted is He, is none other than the perfections of the soul, and that is through sincerity of faith and goodness of following [the Prophet]. As He said:

**Commentary on His words, exalted is He:**

[37] ﴿Neither your wealth nor your children will bring you near to Us in nearness, except for one who believes and does righteous deeds. For those there is a double reward for what they have done, and they will be secure in the lofty chambers.﴾

﴿Neither your wealth nor your children will bring you near to Us in nearness﴾, meaning: by the excellence that brings you nearness in closeness. The word ﴿زُلْفى﴾ (*zulfā*, "nearness") is in the accusative case. ﴿Except for one who believes and does righteous deeds, for those there is a double reward﴾, meaning: the multiplied reward. ﴿for what they have done, and they will be secure in the lofty chambers﴾, meaning: there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve. Among the parallels to this verse is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 55] ﴿is Us hastening good things for them? Rather, they do not perceive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 56]. And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So do not let their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them with them in the worldly life and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 55].

(p-4962) Imam Ahmad and Muslim narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[38] ﴿And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them, they are the ones who will be brought forth into the punishment.﴾

﴿And those who strive against Our verses﴾ — that is, by turning people away from them and disparaging them. ﴿Seeking to frustrate them﴾ — that is, intending to defeat them, overcome them, and subdue them. ﴿They are the ones who will be brought forth into the punishment﴾ — that is, they will be brought forth into the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers.﴾

﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾ That is, He will compensate for it, for the springs of His treasuries never run dry, and the clouds of His provision pour down night and day. ﴿And He is the best of providers﴾ That is, the most excellent of them, because He is the Creator of provision and the Creator of the means by which the one who is provided for benefits from the provision. Abu Ya'la narrated from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, after your time there will come a time of oppression, in which the wealthy man will bite on what is in his hand out of fear of spending." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it.﴾ Mujahid said: Let none of you misinterpret this verse, ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it,﴾ when one has what sustains him; let him be moderate in it, for provision is apportioned.

(p-4963) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[40–41] ﴿And [mention] the Day when He will gather them all, then He will say to the angels, "Did these worship you?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our Guardian, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾ [Saba': 41].

﴿And [mention] the Day when He will gather them all, then He will say to the angels, "Did these worship you?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our Guardian, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾ [Saba': 41]. Al-Zamakhshari said: This speech is addressed to the angels and is a rebuke to the disbelievers, and it comes in the manner of the well-known proverb: "It is you I mean, but hear, O neighbour" (إيّاكَ أعْنِي واسْمَعِي يا جارَةُ). Similar to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116]. And He, glory be to Him, knew that the angels and Jesus were free of blame and innocent of what was directed at them by the question which came in the form of an affirmation (taqrir). The purpose is that He says and they respond, He asks and they answer, so that their rebuke is more severe, their reproach more eloquent, their shame greater, and their humiliation more binding. The narrating of this serves as kindness to whoever hears it and as a deterrent to whoever is told about it. End.

The specification of the angels is because they are the noblest of the rivals (al-andad) in the view of the Arab polytheists, and because their worship is the origin and root of polytheism, since they claimed that the idols are in the forms of the exalted, honoured celestial beings, so that they would be intercessors for them. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did these worship you?﴾ means: Was that by your permission? As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?﴾ [al-Furqan: 17]. And as He, exalted is He, says to Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?" He said, "Exalted are You"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116]. Thus the angels say (p-4964): ﴿Exalted are You!﴾ [Saba': 41], meaning: You are high and sanctified above having any god with You. ﴿You are our Guardian, not them﴾ [Saba': 41], meaning: You are the one whom we take as ally, besides them, since there is no alliance between us and them, so we disown them before You. By affirming the allegiance to Allah and the enmity to the disbelievers, they demonstrated their innocence of approving of being worshipped by them. Their saying: ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾ [Saba': 41], meaning: the devils (al-shayatin), because they were the ones who made the worship of idols seem fair to them and led them astray. The first pronoun in their saying: ﴿most of them were believers in them﴾ [Saba': 41] refers to humankind or to the polytheists, and "most" (al-akthar) is in the sense of "all"; the second pronoun refers to the jinn.

(p-4963) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[40–41] ﴿And [mention] the Day when He will gather them all, then He will say to the angels, "Did these worship you?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our Guardian, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾ [Saba': 41].

﴿And [mention] the Day when He will gather them all, then He will say to the angels, "Did these worship you?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our Guardian, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾ [Saba': 41]. Al-Zamakhshari said: This speech is addressed to the angels and is a rebuke to the disbelievers, and it comes in the manner of the well-known proverb: "It is you I mean, but hear, O neighbour" (إيّاكَ أعْنِي واسْمَعِي يا جارَةُ). Similar to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116]. And He, glory be to Him, knew that the angels and Jesus were free of blame and innocent of what was directed at them by the question which came in the form of an affirmation (taqrir). The purpose is that He says and they respond, He asks and they answer, so that their rebuke is more severe, their reproach more eloquent, their shame greater, and their humiliation more binding. The narrating of this serves as kindness to whoever hears it and as a deterrent to whoever is told about it. End.

The specification of the angels is because they are the noblest of the rivals (al-andad) in the view of the Arab polytheists, and because their worship is the origin and root of polytheism, since they claimed that the idols are in the forms of the exalted, honoured celestial beings, so that they would be intercessors for them. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did these worship you?﴾ means: Was that by your permission? As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?﴾ [al-Furqan: 17]. And as He, exalted is He, says to Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?" He said, "Exalted are You"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116]. Thus the angels say (p-4964): ﴿Exalted are You!﴾ [Saba': 41], meaning: You are high and sanctified above having any god with You. ﴿You are our Guardian, not them﴾ [Saba': 41], meaning: You are the one whom we take as ally, besides them, since there is no alliance between us and them, so we disown them before You. By affirming the allegiance to Allah and the enmity to the disbelievers, they demonstrated their innocence of approving of being worshipped by them. Their saying: ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾ [Saba': 41], meaning: the devils (al-shayatin), because they were the ones who made the worship of idols seem fair to them and led them astray. The first pronoun in their saying: ﴿most of them were believers in them﴾ [Saba': 41] refers to humankind or to the polytheists, and "most" (al-akthar) is in the sense of "all"; the second pronoun refers to the jinn.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[42] ﴿So on that Day, none of you will have power to benefit or harm one another.﴾ And We will say to those who did wrong, ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.﴾

﴿So on that Day, none of you will have power to benefit or harm one another.﴾ That is, because the whole matter on that Day belongs to Allah, since the abode is an abode of recompense, and the One who recompenses is He alone. Abu al-Su'ud said: This is among what will be said to the angels when they respond by declaring Allah far above and disassociating themselves from what the disbelievers attributed to them.
